title: Per-chunk render cost of a streaming reply grows with the reply's length
observed: Faux 8-char chunks, headless, main 7aa37ba: 37k-char reply streams in ~6s, 149k-char reply in ~64s (4x text, ~11x time; ~1.3ms vs ~3.4ms per chunk). On a CI runner the 149k reply took >90s. In hooks/auto-compact-threshold on CI, three ~35k-char turns took 16s, 20s and >21s: the per-chunk cost may also grow with the whole transcript, not only the current reply (not measured separately).
expected: Roughly constant per-chunk cost, so streaming time scales linearly with reply length. Not user-visible at real model rates (tens of tokens/s), but it slows long faux scenarios.
evidence: CI run 37441947945 qa-headless context-overflow timeout screen (27.8k tokens at 91s); local timings from drive.py run logs

fix.note: Each frame re-wrapped the whole streamed reply (wrapMultiline, twice per message in fullscreen: layoutViewport and View) and, in fullscreen, re-set the viewport with the whole transcript (measuring every committed row). Now the live block wraps only the bytes a delta added (streamWrapCache, a resumable ansi.Wrap held to the full re-wrap at every split point) and the fullscreen viewport is handed only the rows on screen. Headless xterm-dark, context-overflow: 150k-char reply streamed in 12s (was 63s). Benchmark per delta, fullscreen: 0.51ms at 10k/40k/150k chars and with 20k committed rows (was 0.85/1.8/5.5ms; 19.5-24ms with 20k rows).
